meta.subject: Teach
meta.summary: Teach uses separate investigation and learning-design agents to turn a finished build into an evidence-backed local learning module.

areas.name: Teach orchestrator
areas.role: Starts the two agents and passes only validated data between them.

areas.name: Build Investigator
areas.role: Reads the conversation and code to establish what is true and relevant.

areas.name: Learning Designer
areas.role: Turns the validated facts into a lesson an 18-year-old can understand.

areas.name: Local output
areas.role: Validates the lesson and opens the finished page on the builder's computer.

problem.summary: One prompt was responsible for both understanding unfamiliar code and teaching it, which encouraged a polished summary without a deep, evidence-backed mental model.

build.summary: Teach now separates factual investigation from learning design and validates the evidence handoff before rendering the module.

system_flow.label: Run Teach
system_flow.detail: The Teach skill creates one output folder and starts the evidence-first workflow.

system_flow.label: Map the build
system_flow.detail: A fresh agent follows the conversation and code, keeps relevant technologies, and records evidence and uncertainties.

system_flow.label: Design the lesson
system_flow.detail: A different agent receives the validated map and chooses the learning goal, real example, simple diagram, and recall question.

system_flow.label: Check and render
system_flow.detail: Python rejects unsupported claims or malformed lesson data, then embeds the approved lesson into one HTML file.

system_flow.label: Open locally
system_flow.detail: A local-only server lets the builder read the finished module in a browser without publishing the page.

technologies.name: JSON
technologies.job: Carries the evidence map and lesson between the two agents and the renderer.
technologies.relevance: The learner needs to see that facts are handed over in a checked structure instead of hidden in another free-form prompt.

technologies.name: Python
technologies.job: Validates both JSON files and builds the final page.
technologies.relevance: It is the deterministic gate between agent-written data and the page the learner sees.

technologies.name: HTML
technologies.job: Stores the complete interactive learning module that opens in the browser.
technologies.relevance: It explains what the final artifact is and why it can remain local.

important_decisions.summary: The Learning Designer does not receive the full repository or conversation, preventing it from silently changing the investigator's facts.
Relevant technology explanations moved into the system step where each tool performs work.

discarded_details.detail: Decorative page styling and incidental implementation libraries
discarded_details.reason: They do not change the learner's picture of how Teach turns evidence into a local module.

evidence.source: Builder feedback: separate code understanding from learning-module creation
evidence.supports: The previous combined prompt explained the product but did not create a deep learning module.
Teach orchestrates two isolated agents and validates the handoff between them.
The first agent inspects conversation, code, system boundaries, technologies, and relevance.
The evidence handoff has deterministic structure, area, flow, and evidence checks.
The second agent receives the validated map and designs the learning experience without reopening the code.
The module contains a learning goal, worked example, area-labelled flow, embedded technology explanations, and recall check.
Lesson evidence, system areas, and technology names are checked against the build map.
The builder embeds validated lesson JSON into the standalone HTML shell.
The generated module is served on a local address for the browser.
